subject: Post-call: parity sprint proposal — open vs proprietary for reconciliation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintegrate.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo + next steps

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — it was helpful to see the routing/fallback flow and the console traces. A quick recap from our side and what we need to proceed:

- Use case: automated payments reconciliation for mid-market merchants (high variety of bank statement formats, lots of OCR noise).
- Key success metrics for our team: entity recall on payee and account numbers (goal >= 96%), end-to-end match rate for transaction pairs (goal >= 92%), and false-positive rate < 3%.
- Constraints: throughput (peak ~300 reqs/sec), average latency target <200ms request-to-first-token for live UI flows, and strict PII handling — anything logged must be redacted.
- Timeline: we'd like to run a 4-week POC starting in mid-Oct if possible.

Can you share the recommended model shortlist, the prompt sets you’d run, and an initial acceptance checklist we can align on? Also want to understand risk: if we move from our proprietary baseline to an open model, where do you expect regressions (entity recall, hallucination types), and what mitigations do you propose?

I’m looping in Mike (procurement) and can get a PO once we agree on scope and cost.

Thanks,
Alicia

--
Alicia Gomez
Head of Product
Fintegrate Payments
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo + next steps

Alicia — great to connect. Quick reply with the shortlist and a pragmatic plan so we can align on the POC scope.

Shortlist (recommended order to trial):
1) OpenModelX-13B (QLoRA + 4-bit quant) — strong latency/cost tradeoff, good NER baseline after prompt tuning.
2) Llama2-70B (8-bit) — higher raw recall for entity extraction in some enterprise datasets, higher cost.
3) Redwood-Prod-Opt-v1 (proprietary baseline) — what you’re currently comparing to; stable in-domain performance and tuned rerankers.

Acceptance & gating (proposal):
- Entity recall (payee, account, routing): target >= 96% for production pass, gate for POC success >= 92%.
- Pair match F1: prod gate >= 92%, POC gate >= 88%.
- Hallucination rate (defined as asserted account numbers not present in source): < 1% for production, POC threshold 2.5%.
- Latency: median time-to-first-token <= 200ms for a 256-token context. For larger batches we’ll measure p95 token latency separately.
- Cost signal: projected token cost per 1k requests for candidate model must be <= 1.8x of Redwood-Prod baseline to justify migration risk.

Planned deliverables for the 4-week POC we propose:
- Week 0 (kickoff): finalize prompt bundle + sample dataset (you can drop 5k representative records to the Drive link).
- Week 1: quickscan benchmark across the three candidates (we’ll run the attached quickscan CSV) to surface obvious gaps.
- Week 2: prompt & prompt-ensemble tuning + lightweight QLoRA where feasible.
- Week 3: A/B test on 10k withheld queries (stat test on recall + match rate) and run hallucination analysis.
- Week 4: parity readout and recommended next steps (canary or dedicated capacity).

Attachments I’m sending: fintegrate-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (starter prompts), redwood-bench-quickscan-20261005.csv (initial metrics we’ll compute), parity-sprint-milestones.pdf (schedule & owner list).

Risks & mitigations (short):
- Regression on niche bank formats: mitigate with small in-context examples + targeted prompt templates.
- PII leakage in logs: use private deployment or enable KMS+redaction in Redwood Private; we will redact and only store hash tokens for metrics.
- Cost blowouts under high throughput: we’ll model batching policies and fallbacks to smaller variants for bulk jobs.

Next steps: can we lock a 60-minute kickoff on Tue Oct 12 or Wed Oct 13 (your timezone)? Also, Alicia — if you can confirm the included PO contact (Mike), we’ll attach an estimated POC cost range in the kickoff note.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@fintegrate.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / demo + next steps

Adding a few technical specifics on measurement and regression controls so we have a concrete plan for Week 2/3: 

Measurement plan (what we’ll compute):
- Exact match and token-level F1 for extracted entities (payee, account_no, routing_no).
- Record-level pair match (precision/recall/F1) for reconciliation pairs.
- Hallucination detection via token overlap + negative sampling (we will synthesize 500 negative cases to measure false assertion rate).
- Operational metrics: qps, median latency, p95 latency, and token cost per 1k requests.

Technical mitigations if open models underperform: 
- Rerank stage: deterministic reranker that filters candidate extractions against OCR-derived tokens (cheap step that recovers recall).
- Lightweight fine-tune (QLoRA) using ~2k labeled examples if prompt engineering hits a ceiling — we’ll include cost/time estimates in the kickoff pack.
- Guardrail layer: require match confidence threshold before auto-close; everything below goes to human review queue.

Experiment size & stats:
- A/B on 10k records (5k control = Redwood-Prod, 5k treatment = open candidate); with expected baseline recall 0.92 and minimum detectable uplift/downtick 0.03, this should be adequately powered.

Operational ask from you (Fintegrate):
- Drop a redacted sample set (5k) to the Drive folder we linked.
- Identify a PO contact for POC provisioning (Alicia flagged Mike).
- Confirm whether PII must stay on-prem (if yes, we’ll recommend Redwood Private).

I’ll prepare the scripts we’ll run for quickscan (the CSV lists metrics + tags).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
